To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the response of a lake food web to a top-down perturbation is different in a temperate lake than in a tropical lake.
the effects of fish on the structure and functioning of food webs are greater in temperate lakes, and that this is related to differences in stoichiometry.
fish-induced trophic casc- ades are greater in temperate lakes than in tropical lakes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of food web structure in regulating nutrient cycling and primary production in lakes.
the effects of the fish presence on the structure of food-webs and the consequences of this on nutrient availability for algae in temperate and tropic- al lakes.
the effects of fish predation on plankton community and nutrient recycling in lakes of temperate and tropics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tropical lakes are more sensitive to fish predation than temperate lakes, but this statement is based on very few experiments and is not supported by any mechanistic explanation.
the food web of tropical lakes is less responsive to the top-down control of fish, but more responsive to the bottom-up control of nutrients, than that of temperate lakes.
the trophic cascading theory is not applicable to tropical lakes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

food-web structure alteration by fish has greater effects on phytoplankton biomass and composition in temperate than tropical lakes, and this is likely due to differences in nutrient availability and stoichiometric constraints.

the stoichiometric response of food webs to fish-induced changes in structure is different in tropical and temperate lakes, and that this response is likely to be driven by differences in nutrient limitation between the ecosystems.
the stoichiometry of food webs is a crucial factor to consider for a better understanding of the functioning of tropical and temperate lakes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should consider bottom-up mechanisms when comparing temperate and tropical systems.
we should not consider the same mechanisms to explain food-web functioning and structure in temperate and in tropical lakes.
stoichiometry should be considered as a major factor to explain food-web functioning and its response to environmental change.
